_comment: Comprehension questions shown after a story. Single source of truth.
Every answer is stated in content/ai-ready/*.md, and source_note says
where, so a reader who disagrees can check.
Regenerate the seeds with: python3 ai/scripts/export_seed_data.py

questions.question: When was the Dome of the Rock completed?
questions.explanation: It was built by order of the Umayyad Caliph Abd al-Malik ibn Marwan and completed in 691-692 CE.

questions.question: Who rebuilt the walls that surround the Old City today?
questions.explanation: The present walls were rebuilt in the 16th century CE under the Ottoman Sultan Suleiman the Magnificent. Much of what they enclose is far older.
questions.source_note: Short overview and timeline, Ottoman era

questions.question: How many quarters does the Old City contain?
questions.explanation: Four: the Muslim, Christian, Armenian and Jewish quarters. Eight is the number of historic gates.

questions.question: When did Caliph Umar ibn al-Khattab enter Jerusalem?
questions.explanation: He entered peacefully in 638 CE at the request of Patriarch Sophronius, and issued a covenant guaranteeing the inhabitants their lives, property and places of worship.

questions.question: Who ordered the building of the Church of the Nativity?
options: Constantine I and his mother Helena
questions.explanation: Constantine I and Helena ordered it in the 4th century CE; it was completed around 339 CE. Justinian I rebuilt parts of it in the 6th century after damage.

questions.question: Roughly how far is Bethlehem from Jerusalem?
questions.explanation: About 10 km south of Jerusalem, on a plateau roughly 775 m above sea level.

questions.question: Which crafts is Bethlehem best known for?
questions.explanation: Olive-wood objects and mother-of-pearl work, alongside Palestinian embroidery.

questions.question: In which year was the Church of the Nativity removed from UNESCO's List of World Heritage in Danger?
options: It is still on the list
questions.explanation: It was inscribed on the World Heritage List in 2012 and removed from the danger list in 2019, once the required conservation work was completed.

questions.question: Who rebuilt the city in 27 BCE and gave it the name Sebastia?
questions.explanation: Herod the Great rebuilt it and named it Sebastia, the Greek form of the title of the emperor Augustus, in his honour.

questions.question: What was the city called before it was named Sebastia?
questions.explanation: Its ancient Canaanite name was Shomron - Samaria - and it was the capital of the northern Kingdom of Israel in the 9th century BCE.

questions.question: The Mosque of Nabi Yahya was converted from which building?
options: A Byzantine cathedral rebuilt by the Crusaders
questions.explanation: A cathedral was built in the Byzantine period at the site associated with John the Baptist, rebuilt by the Crusaders, and partly converted into the Mosque of Nabi Yahya under the Mamluks.
questions.source_note: Main landmarks and timeline, Ayyubid and Mamluk eras

questions.question: Which Roman structure at Sebastia is among the best preserved in Palestine?
questions.explanation: The colonnaded street, flanked by two rows of massive columns that once carried porticoes for merchants.
